channel.title: Belyakov Consult · Articles
channel.description: Practical notes on data quality, BI, architecture, governance and GovTech, written around real decision problems.

item.title: Which BI platform to choose: a ten-criteria comparison map
item.description: Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, Looker and SAP Analytics Cloud in one interactive map: from the main strength to what most often makes the work harder.

item.title: Document type can matter more than the number itself
item.description: Why a document number alone is not enough for reliable identification in data exchange, and what to add so a matching number does not become an error.

item.title: One person, three records: register duplicates
item.description: Why one person shows up in a register several times, what it does to reports and payments, and where to fix duplicates.

item.title: BI should not be the place where source systems are repaired
item.description: Why cleaning and stitching data inside Power BI makes reports fragile, and which part of that work belongs in the data model.

item.title: 98% complete does not mean 98% quality
item.description: Why a high completeness rate says little about whether registry data is usable, and which checks reveal its real quality.

item.title: Data quality dashboard: don't hide the problem in an average
item.description: Four indicators on the first screen, a matrix instead of one number, a target set by the data owner and a PDF report. Plus a demo on synthetic data.

item.title: Three levels of data quality in registers
item.description: What ISO 8000-8 says about syntactic, semantic and pragmatic quality, and why registers need all three.

item.title: You can see data governance when numbers conflict
item.description: Two teams bring different figures, and both are right. What that moment reveals about data governance and the four questions to start with.
